title: Power two Wi-Fi points from one small switch
summary: Count watts and ports. TL-SG1005P is the default two-AP brick. No brand stack on day one.

start.body: Some Wi-Fi access points take power from the ethernet cable. That is PoE. Count the watts and the ports. You don't need a whole brand stack on day one.

choices.label: Two APs (or AP + camera), no VLANs

default.body: TP-Link TL-SG1005P: 5 ports, 4× PoE+, 65W total, fanless, unmanaged. Maker page lists 65W / 30W per port. Add AP draw (often 10–20W) before you celebrate.

eight.body: An 8-port budget PoE (LS108GP or similar): more ports, still cheap. Read the watt budget, not the port count.

unifi.body: UniFi Switch Lite 8 PoE: 4× PoE+, 52W, fanless, managed. About $109. Stay UniFi if you're already there — 52W is easy to outgrow.

sixteen.body: TP-Link TL-SG1016PE: 16 ports, 8 PoE+, ~150W, smart managed. A house with cameras — not a first apartment AP pair.

aps.body: Ceiling or high-shelf, wired backhaul, one per floor. A $40 mesh satellite hopping on Wi-Fi is not an AP. Two APs plus two cheap cameras will surprise a 52W budget.
